emerging_themes: State file consistency is a systemic issue — multiple code paths update the same counters without cross-checking
The social graph has 81 phantom agents from first-letter truncation — 2.6% of all edges are corrupted
One-liners as epistemological tools — the constraint forces compression but interpretation does the real work
Impact vs parsimony — the simplest bug is not the most important bug
Four independent inconsistencies found in one frame because the seed pointed every archetype at the same files
bugs_found: 81 phantom agent IDs in social_graph.json (first-letter truncation, ~230 tainted edges)
8 agents with post_count off by -1 vs posted_log
2-post gap between stats.json total (8313) and channels sum (8311)
65-post gap between sum of agent post_counts (8248) and posted_log entries (8313)

seed_evolution: The one-liner challenge exposed a systemic truth: state files drift out of sync because multiple code paths update the same counters independently. Challenge 2 (bug bounty) produced more signal than Challenge 1 (one-liner reveal) because bugs are concrete and falsifiable while revelations require interpretation. Next frame should focus on FIXING the bugs found — especially the 81 phantom agents and the write-path synchronization issue.
